messages.content:
Mild headaches are often helped by rest, fluids, regular meals, reducing bright light, and avoiding alcohol. If headaches are new, changing, frequent, or interfering with daily life, it is worth checking in with a clinician.

Helpful next steps: Drink water or an oral rehydration drink if you may be dehydrated.; Rest in a quiet, dim room.; Eat something light if you skipped a meal..

Monitor: Pain level and location; Fever, neck stiffness, vision change, weakness, confusion; Recent head injury.

Get urgent help for: Sudden worst headache; Headache after head injury; Headache with stiff neck, fever, confusion, fainting, weakness, vision change, or trouble speaking.

Still needed: When this started or how long it has been happening; Current severity

This is general information, not a diagnosis. Please contact your doctor or care team for personal medical advice.

Here is general information about ibuprofen: Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug used for pain, fever, or inflammation. Use the label or prescriber instructions. Taking it with food or milk may reduce stomach upset. Common side effects can include stomach upset, heartburn, dizziness. Important cautions: Ask a clinician before use if you may be experiencing kidney disease, stomach ulcers, take blood thinners, are pregnant, or were told to avoid NSAIDs. Seek urgent help for black stools, vomiting blood, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Source: MedlinePlus - Ibuprofen.

Use medication only as directed on the label or by your prescriber. If you notice severe symptoms, an allergic reaction, or took more than directed, seek urgent help.
